name: South Lanarkshire
title: South Lanarkshire —
title_em: New Lanark and the Clyde Valley.
tagline: A UNESCO mill village, orchards on the Clyde and the town where Wallace began his rebellion.
summary: South Lanarkshire has the UNESCO World Heritage Site of New Lanark, a cotton mill village founded in 1786 and run by social reformer Robert Owen. The Clyde Valley is known for orchards and gardens.
Hamilton, East Kilbride and Rutherglen are the main towns, while Lanark is the place where William Wallace is said to have begun his rebellion in 1297.
